Subject: POC plan & risk tracker — success criteria, timeline, blocking issues

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo today. Per our call, I wanted to share a concise POC plan (attached) and capture the initial success criteria, timeline, owners, and known risks so we can move quickly.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for your real-time chat summarization pipeline at 90th-percentile latency < 250ms and token cost <= $0.0015/token for sustained load.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Functional: generated summaries match your evaluation rubric on the 200 sample prompts (>= 85% pass).
2) Performance: p90 latency < 250ms for 1k concurrent sessions; mean cost per 1k tokens meets target.
3) Stability: no memory / crash events during 48-hour soak run.

Evaluation plan / deliverables:
- You provide 200 sample prompts and rubric (Samir to confirm by 7/16).
- Redwood to run side-by-side tests and provide per-prompt scorecards (deliverable: scorecard CSV).
- Performance run: 48-hour soak with synthetic traffic + representative KV cache usage.

Timeline (draft):
- 7/16: Acme sends samples + rubric.
- 7/20: Redwood delivers test harness + initial config.
- 7/21–7/23: 48-hour soak + regression checks.
- 7/24: Checkpoint call to review results; decide go/no-go.

Owners:
- Acme: Alex (POC lead), Samir (infra/security contact)
- Redwood: Marissa (sales), Rishi (AM), Dylan (CS engineer), Vivek (SRE backup)

Known risks / blocking items (initial):
- Data egress & VPC peering rules — Samir to confirm network constraints.
- Long-lived session token rotation observed in similar customers (possible stateful bug).

\Next steps:
1) Samir: confirm samples + security checklist by 7/16.
2) Rishi: schedule engineering kickoff 7/20 and confirm required infra access.
3) Redwood: prepare test harness and runnable POC plan (attached: POC-plan-v1.pdf, SLA-questions.docx).

If anything here looks off, call it out and we’ll adjust. Proposed checkpoint: Fri 7/24 11:00 AM PT (invite to follow).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and plan. A few notes from Acme:

- We’ll send the 200 samples + rubric by 7/16 EOD.
- Success criteria: we may tighten the functional pass threshold to 88% for production parity; I'll confirm.
- Security: we require evidence of data handling + sample SOC / controls (I attached our security questionnaire and our internal security contact Samir).

Blocking concern: our infra team flagged potential issues with VPC egress and outbound NAT for token streaming to hosted endpoints. If Redwood’s hosted endpoints require open outbound ranges, that may be a showstopper. Can you confirm the network requirements and whether there’s a private endpoint option?

Also: during our internal spike we saw stateful session degradation after ~24 hours (requests start returning 500s unless worker is restarted). Not sure if related to token rotation, but worth tracking as a high-priority risk.

I attached our security brief (company-security.pdf).

—Alex

Following up with findings from our spike: 

- Reproduction: we reproduced the 24-hour degradation on a long-lived session with continuous token streaming. Root cause appears to be token rotation + KV cache eviction interplay on our inference workers that leads to stale auth headers being retried until the worker hits an internal rate-limit and returns 500s.

- Workaround (short-term): reduce session TTL to 12 hours and restart worker every 12 hours. This avoids the rotation window.

- Fix (medium-term): patch inbound token rotation flow in the runtime — PR target: 2026-07-20 EOD for the patch and canary. If canary is green, we’ll push to POC fleet on 7/21 morning.

- Network: Vivek — we can provide a list of egress CIDR blocks and a private VPC peering guide by 7/19.

Attachments: trace-log.txt (small excerpt of logs showing rotation failure).

If the patch slips, escalate per Rishi’s plan to SRE — Vivek, please stand by to allocate a hotfix rollout.

—Dylan
